source_review.notes: Checked every structured reference for identity, date or edition, and cited scope. NIST SP 800-218 version 1.1 is the February 2022 final SSDF and supports integrating high-level secure-development practices into each SDLC. Current official GitHub ruleset documentation supports required checks, expected check sources, strict and loose synchronization, reviews, and layered enforcement. Approved SLSA specification 1.2 supports provenance as verifiable production information, separate existence, authenticity, accuracy and anti-forgery properties, and verification against expectations. Current DORA continuous-delivery guidance supports fast feedback, reliable automated tests, pervasive security, and continuous deployability. Verified Humble/Farley and Meszaros bibliographic metadata for delivery-pipeline and test-result foundations. Checked 2026-09-06.

evidence: Defined subject, policy, mandatory claim set, evidence bundle, per-claim three-valued evaluator, aggregate gate, freshness age, threshold, accepted and violating sets, and false-acceptance observations before use.
Checked set membership, quantifiers, cases, conjunction semantics, time differences, inequalities, intersections, and all GitHub math delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: T, F, and U are policy evaluation states and not probabilities.

evidence: Executed quality-gate-model under CPython 3.14.4 and matched seven exact output lines with empty stderr and exit status zero.
Recomputed healthy age as 20 <= 60, expired age as 100 > 60, zero and one critical findings against maximum zero, and waiver time 120 <= 130.
Checked the freshness exercise: 30-hour provenance exceeds a 24-hour window and is incomplete under the chapter model; one critical finding makes the aggregate fail despite missing provenance.
Checked the 200 ms inclusive threshold accepts equality and rejects values strictly above 200 when measurement is known.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Coverage, vulnerability, latency, and delivery scenarios are illustrative and make no empirical claim.

evidence: Exhausted the three-valued aggregate: any F gives fail; absent F, all T gives pass; absent F and not all T implies at least one U and gives incomplete.
Checked freshness predicate t_d - t_e <= Delta_c and stated equality, clock, and time-source requirements.
Checked inclusive upper threshold x <= theta differs from strict x < theta at equality.
Checked observed false acceptances A intersect V and retained the limited-oracle qualification.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The aggregation is a policy definition; no statistical confidence or universal risk rate is inferred.

evidence: Reviewed exact threshold equality, just-above values, measurement uncertainty, empty evidence, missing and malformed reports, stale evidence, wrong revision, wrong artifact, unavailable platforms, skipped versus not-applicable, and conflicting results.

Reviewed absolute and relative debt, baseline resets, coverage gaming, missing assertions, advisory-data freshness, severity and reachability, human approval, policy transitions, short-circuiting, and slow-gate feedback effects.

Reviewed untrusted producers, self-modifying policy, signing-key exposure, forged provenance, permanent and repeated waivers, expiry, revocation, compensating controls, false acceptance, false rejection, Goodhart effects, and metric gaming.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Production thresholds require domain risk, measurement protocol, uncertainty treatment, and accountable ownership.

evidence: Traced exact revision or artifact identity through evidence envelope, authenticated issuer, method and configuration, environment, inputs, time, normalized predicate, aggregate decision, and audit record.
Checked missing, stale, unavailable, unverifiable, and ambiguous evidence can never yield pass.
Checked absolute limits, relative baselines, policy versions, scope rules, and threshold units remain explicit.
Checked waivers preserve the original fail or incomplete outcome and require subject scope, authority, rationale, controls, expiry, and revocation conditions.
invariant_checking.notes: A consistent gate cannot make incomplete tools, weak tests, or poor claims complete.

evidence: Reviewed aggregation by exhaustive disjoint cases over mandatory evaluators and confirmed unknown cannot pass.
Reviewed the a6 versus a7 subject-binding counterexample and confirmed filename equality is irrelevant.
Reviewed threshold boundary behavior for inclusive upper limits and retained measurement-uncertainty qualification.
Reviewed waiver preservation and confirmed overwriting failure with pass destroys audit, expiry, and remediation meaning.
proof_review.notes: The proofs establish evaluator consistency and counterexamples, not truth of underlying quality or security claims.

evidence: Audited uses of quality, proof, pass, fail, incomplete, true, false, unknown, required, authenticated, trusted, current, fresh, complete, verified, and safe.
Confirmed formal policy semantics, official current behavior, professional judgment, illustrative scenarios, proxy limitations, and local execution are clearly separated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter repeatedly distinguishes control evidence from universal software correctness.

evidence: Executed the sole practical snippet under CPython 3.14.4 with declared exact stdout, empty stderr, and exit status zero.
Confirmed pass, missing-evidence incomplete, critical-finding fail, stale-evidence incomplete, valid waiver, coverage limitation, and same-revision requirement behavior.
Confirmed all repository, vulnerability, benchmark, coverage, release, suppression, and incident cases are hypothetical teaching situations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No real source, artifact, scanner, ruleset, SLSA verifier, signing service, delivery pipeline, benchmark, or production gate was evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the complete decision chain from claims and exact subjects through evidence envelopes, three-valued outcomes, authenticated provenance, threshold semantics, absolute and relative limits, composition, scheduling, policy governance, waivers, explanation, and control evaluation. Tool activity, evidence, claim truth, and admission remain distinct.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed failures across wrong subjects, skipped checks, stale reports, arbitrary thresholds, weak coverage proxies, baseline gaming, advisory changes, issuer forgery, signing-key exposure, candidate-controlled policy, mid-run policy changes, missing triggers, manual waits, unactionable failures, unbounded waivers, suppressed findings, retries, metric gaming, and enforcement drift. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified undergraduate progression from exact vocabulary and one mismatched-provenance case through three-valued gate notation, four bounded arguments, one executable seven-outcome model, eight trade-off pairs, eighteen misconceptions, ten distinct cases, and five exercises progressing from definitions through outcome derivation, trust diagnosis, risk-tier design, and proxy-gate evaluation.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. Standards and official documentation, abstract gate logic, deterministic examples, hypothetical cases, and one local model execution do not establish test adequacy, scanner completeness, vulnerability absence, provenance trust, policy correctness, artifact safety, regulatory compliance, production risk reduction, or gate effectiveness.
